assets_and_boundaries.summary: Four plant process-cell LANs (10.20.10.0/24 through 10.20.13.0/24, VLANs 10-13) and four HMI LANs (10.20.50.0/24 through 10.20.53.0/24, VLANs 50-53) meet at MET-PLANT. The named access segments are logical segments, not independently specified switch appliances.
SCADA, engineering, historian, MQTT, and OT services occupy separate VLANs 20, 21, 22, 23, and 30 behind MET-OT-CORE; the DMZ, simulated enterprise, and attack-test LANs meet at MET-OT-DMZ.
Reservoir and raw-water LANs (10.20.14.0/24 and 10.20.15.0/24) connect to MET-OT-WAN through logical IPsec VTI overlays over the shared 172.31.255.0/24 underlay; overlay links are not GNS3 cables.

asset_boundaries.generated_policy: The compiler emits source/destination CIDR, protocol, and destination-port allows on each declared router path; reverse established/related traffic is accepted, and generated zones and rulesets default to drop. Same-subnet paths bypass router policy. Baseline rules cannot allow the attack-test LAN; temporary experiment exceptions require router configuration and a later restoration attempt.
asset_boundaries.deployment_limit: Building a project compiles and applies router policy only with --configure-routers; console readback checks are part of that application path. These files establish intended generated controls, not that any rule, cable, switch VLAN, route, or tunnel is live.
live_verification_gaps: Actual GNS3 cabling and switch VLAN placement
Service availability, identity checks, command acceptance, and actuation
Any temporary experiment exception currently installed

baseline_flows.reason: The scada-to-plant-dosing allow selects the entire SCADA subnet, so both declared SCADA-subnet hosts inherit network reachability; Modbus service and commands remain separate gates.
The DNP3 baseline allow is routed over the declared WAN-hub/reservoir VTI; live IPsec, OSPF, cables, and outstation service remain unverified.
Engineering-subnet Modbus access is allowed to the intake LAN; the rule is not restricted to this workstation.
The engineering-to-intake CoAP allow covers this declared client and sensor; response integrity and service behavior are separate checks.
Every HMI subnet has a routed MQTT allowance; broker authentication and topic ACLs are additional gates.
Historian-to-SCADA OPC UA is explicitly allowed; declared secure-session and peer-certificate settings still gate access.
SCADA-to-DMZ HTTPS is explicitly allowed; the relay's declared client certificate and writer identity are additional gates.
Enterprise-to-DMZ HTTPS is explicitly allowed to the whole DMZ subnet; relay reader identity and mutual TLS still gate data.
Engineering Modbus allowance selects intake only; an unmatched routed flow meets the generated default drop.
Attack-test traffic has no baseline routed allowance; temporary experiment exceptions may change a run, but no such deployed exception is evidenced.
Both hosts attach to the intake segment, so this is a local Layer 2 path outside the routed firewall; whether the source can issue accepted Modbus requests is unverified.
The selected plan declares a simulated enterprise LAN and its router/switch attachment, but no outside ingress endpoint or path; do not assume an initial foothold from outside.

framework_inspiration.prompt: Determine whether discovery came from an approved engineering or inventory role and whether target scope or rate departed from baseline. The narrower Port Scan sub-technique T0846.001 requires port-probe evidence: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T0846/001/.
Correlate repeated authentication failures with account and source logs before claiming credential compromise. The Mirai Telnet label alone does not prove password guessing.

For Modbus writes or cross-cell MQTT command topics, establish an unapproved source, actual delivery to the intended controller or subscriber, and command or process-state effect. A named write tool or topic is not itself an unauthorized message.
Only map the CoAP branch if a forged response is observed at the receiver and differs from the legitimate sensor report.
Correlate MQTT flood or hping3 traffic with broker, subscriber, controller-polling, or device availability degradation; traffic volume alone does not establish denial of service.

framework_inspiration.technique: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
framework_inspiration.prompt: Distinguish the modeled Merlin HTTPS check-in and result path from legitimate SCADA-to-DMZ telemetry by origin, peer, port, and service identity; do not infer malware deployment.

framework_inspiration.technique: T0869.002 Standard Application Layer Protocol: Publish/Subscribe Protocols
framework_inspiration.prompt: Map only if broker traffic carries adversary command-and-control, not because normal HMI and telemetry paths use MQTT.

owasp_risk_conditions_and_prompts.prompt: Check whether any unintended host in a permitted source LAN can use its LAN-wide Modbus or CoAP conduit, and whether same-VLAN flows need a separate control. These declarations do not demonstrate misuse.
Check broker client/topic authorization for cross-cell HMI publishes and distinguish network reachability from permission to issue a command.
Check whether exercise traffic interrupts delivery, polling, or operator view; no availability impact follows from the catalog names alone.
If the HTTP HMI login is assessed, check automated-guessing controls and session/account attribution; MQTT and SSH brute-force labels do not establish an HMI web flaw.
If HMI web actions expose cell setpoints, verify each user and cell is authorized for the requested action. The inventory does not show handler authorization logic.

If the HTTPS telemetry relay exposes API functions, verify SCADA writer and enterprise reader identities are enforced per function, not inferred from network reachability. No API flaw is established by the inventory.
HMI uses HTTP Basic on a plain ThreadingHTTPServer at TCP/8080. Assess whether authorized network users or observers could read credentials in transit; no interception or login was tested.

steps.protocol_port: TCP service probe, dynamic source port to TCP/502
steps.network_status: permitted in declared baseline for TCP/502; other default scan ports may be blocked
steps.action: Optional scanner-inspired discovery of the intake PLC service from the assumed engineering foothold, with target and port narrowed to TCP/502.
steps.gate: The catalog tool runs on its invoking host; its presence on engineering and any live response are unverified.

observable.expected: A service probe from 10.20.21.10 to TCP/502 before any coil write
observable.provenance: generic behavioral; tool options and path are source-supported
observable.caveat: An authorized inventory or engineering check can look identical; no scan is claimed to have run.

attack_mapping.assessment: Conditional port-probe behavior if this optional discovery stage occurs; no scan observed.

steps.protocol_port: Modbus TCP, dynamic source port to TCP/502
steps.action: Write intake pump-request coil 0; a one-off write can be superseded by the routine control client.
steps.gate: Live route and policy application are unverified; the normal control client also writes coil 0 roughly every 30 seconds.

observable.expected: Modbus coil-0 write sourced from 10.20.21.10, distinguished from routine 10.20.21.20 writes by source and cadence
observable.provenance: generic behavioral; routine writer source is code-supported
observable.caveat: An authorized engineer or lab exercise may issue the same write.

attack_mapping.assessment: Hypothesized unauthorized command if source and write are unapproved; no attack observed.

steps.protocol_port: lab EtherNet/IP TCP/44818 setup and cyclic UDP/2222; dynamic source ports
steps.network_status: same declared intake VLAN; routed firewall bypassed
steps.action: PLC sends requested output and uses confirmed drive state with the valve state to advance the small process model.
steps.gate: Drive and valve must be available and confirm the commanded state; standby can take over if duty is not running.

observable.expected: actuator_state_changed plus later flow_rate, level_percent and quality_percent changes
observable.caveat: Drive event has no source IP or timestamp; SCADA does not publish intake discrete-input confirmation.

scenarios.simulator_effect: Confirmed pump-and-valve operation changes bounded modeled flow, level and quality; register 4 intake setpoint does not drive this model.
scenarios.hypothetical_physical_implication: An analogous real pump command could alter intake operation; this lab model cannot establish hydraulic or water-quality consequences.

defender_hypothesis.support: A 10.20.21.10 coil write followed by duty or standby confirmation and a process trend, especially outside the routine client's cycle.
defender_hypothesis.refute: No accepted coil write, normal client immediately overwrites it, or no confirmed drive-and-valve response.
defender_hypothesis.benign: Authorized engineering adjustment or bounded testbed control exercise.

scenarios.t_minus_1: Unknown: no external ingress or acquisition of the assumed internal foothold is established by reviewed source.

scenarios.family: HMI web credential misuse and SCADA command bridge
scenarios.assumed_foothold: MET-ENGINEERING-01 (10.20.21.10) is controlled and a valid dosing HMI web credential has been acquired; neither event is established.

steps.protocol_port: HTTP Basic, dynamic source port to TCP/8080
steps.action: Authenticated JSON POST to /api/setpoint queues one bounded 0.1-percent-increment request and returns 202 with request_id, not a PLC acknowledgement.
steps.gate: Valid Basic credential, required custom header and JSON body, range and one-pending-command checks.

observable.caveat: The shared web username does not identify the human operator; a legitimate request looks similar.

steps.protocol_port: MQTT, dynamic source port to TCP/1883
steps.action: Publish fresh request_id, cell, device, command, value, unit and timestamp to the dosing command topic.
steps.gate: Broker authentication and per-cell write ACL; MQTT publication can fail or time out.

observable.expected: dosing command topic publication and last_publish_queued_at
observable.provenance: broker log configuration and source-specific HMI state
observable.caveat: Exact broker log fields require live confirmation; queued publication is not controller storage.

steps.protocol_port: MQTT delivery on SCADA-initiated established TCP/1883 session
steps.network_status: stateful return of permitted SCADA-to-broker flow
steps.action: Deliver dosing command to subscribed SCADA bridge; SCADA checks request ID, cell, command, unit, value and age.
steps.gate: SCADA subscription and queue availability; fresh well-formed request; duplicate request IDs replay an ACK without another write.

observable.expected: command request_id/cell; rejection can follow validation, while stored/failed follows the T4 write attempt
observable.caveat: Stored means register write/readback, not confirmed dosing drive operation.

steps.protocol_port: Modbus TCP, dynamic source port to TCP/502
steps.action: Write setpoint register 4 and require matching readback.
steps.gate: PLC reachable and Modbus write/readback succeeds.

observable.point: PLC attachment wire and SCADA status
observable.expected: register-4 write/readback, later setpoint and dose_output_percent
observable.provenance: generic wire behavior plus source-specific SCADA fields
observable.caveat: The PLC does not explicitly log a valid setpoint write.

attack_mapping.assessment: Hypothesized unauthorized command if request is unapproved and reaches the PLC; HTTP 202 alone is insufficient.

steps.protocol_port: lab EtherNet/IP TCP/44818 setup and cyclic UDP/2222
steps.network_status: same declared dosing VLAN; routed firewall bypassed
steps.action: Apply setpoint to modeled dose_output_percent only when pH demand, fresh analyzer, enabled coil and confirmed duty or standby drive coincide.
steps.gate: Analyzer and drive readiness; normal synthetic pH must trigger dosing demand.

observable.point: SCADA status, PLC alarm log and drive stdout
observable.expected: pH, setpoint, dose_output_percent, alarm mask and possible actuator_state_changed
observable.caveat: Natural pH cycle and legitimate operator adjustment can produce the same output sequence.

scenarios.simulator_effect: Stores a dosing setpoint and conditionally changes modeled dose output when a drive confirms running; the analyzer is independent of the drive and there is no chemistry model.
scenarios.hypothetical_physical_implication: An analogous real dosing setpoint change could affect chemical feed, but this simulator does not establish delivered dose or water quality.

defender_hypothesis.support: Correlated HMI request ID, MQTT command, SCADA stored ACK, PLC setpoint readback and conditional dose-output change outside an approved operation.
defender_hypothesis.refute: Rejected/failed ACK, no matching register readback, or no pH demand and no confirmed drive response.
defender_hypothesis.benign: Authorized dosing setpoint adjustment during normal synthetic pH variation.

scenarios.t_minus_1: Unknown: no external ingress or acquisition of the assumed internal foothold is established by reviewed source.

branches.protocol_port: MQTT, dynamic source port to TCP/1883
branches.condition: After validation, and after T4 write/readback for stored or failed outcomes, SCADA publishes request_id, cell, controller, value, timestamp and status; broker authentication and ACL still apply.
branches.observable: SCADA HMI-command log plus ack-topic packet or broker receipt; stored means register readback, not drive confirmation.

branches.protocol_port: MQTT delivery on established HMI-initiated TCP/1883 session
branches.network_status: stateful return of permitted HMI-to-broker flow
branches.condition: HMI accepts only a matching pending request_id, cell, status, controller, timestamp and value before timeout.
branches.observable: HMI /api/status command_status and request_id; a timeout or rejected/failed result cannot be treated as stored.

branches.protocol_port: lab EtherNet/IP TCP/44818 setup and cyclic UDP/2222
branches.condition: Standby requested only when dosing demand, analyzer readiness and enable coil are true and duty drive is not confirmed running.
branches.observable: Standby actuator_state_changed, discrete input and alarms; no actuator origin IP in stdout.

scenarios.branch_order: ACK publication follows validation and, for stored or failed, T4 write/readback. Drive actuation can occur independently of ACK delivery; standby is conditional on duty confirmation.

stage_distinctions.meaning: Locally accepted and queued request only.
Modbus register 4 write succeeded and matching readback was observed.
Dose output is conditional on pH demand, analyzer readiness, enabled coil and duty or standby confirmation.

scenarios.assumed_foothold: MET-OPS-ADMIN-01 (10.20.20.20) is controlled and can run a Modbus client; its declared normal role is RDP client, so malicious control capability is assumed.

steps.protocol_port: Modbus TCP, dynamic source port to TCP/502 via MET-OT-CORE, MET-OT-WAN vti10 and MET-RAW-WATER
steps.network_status: permitted by declared source-subnet scada-modbus rule; live VTI routing unknown
steps.action: Write remote pump-request coil 0; policy's scada selector covers the entire 10.20.20.0/24 subnet, including ops-admin.

steps.protocol_port: lab EtherNet/IP TCP/44818 setup and cyclic UDP/2222
steps.action: RTU sends coil-derived pump request to local drive and exposes requested and confirmed state.
steps.gate: Drive connection and confirmation; output-unconfirmed alarms are delayed by the configured confirmation interval.

defender_hypothesis.refute: No live VTI route, firewall does not apply as declared, or RTU coil and drive status remain unchanged.
defender_hypothesis.benign: Authorized remote commissioning or maintenance from the operations segment.

steps.protocol_port: MQTT, dynamic source port to TCP/1883
steps.action: Publish altered intake telemetry on the sensor's authorized topic; normal code reads PLC values and emits device, sensor, value, unit and timestamp.

observable.expected: metropolis/plant/intake/telemetry value or timestamp diverging from a near-time PLC/SCADA read
observable.provenance: source-specific payload fields and configured broker logging; divergence is a defender inference

steps.protocol_port: MQTT delivery on historian-initiated established TCP/1883 session
steps.network_status: stateful return of permitted historian-to-broker flow
steps.action: Deliver topic under historian's metropolis/# subscription; historian writes received_at, topic and decoded payload to stdout without an intake-value validation step.
steps.gate: Historian subscriber must be connected; broker ACL confines sensor publication to its intake topic.

observable.expected: received_at, topic and payload for the altered intake reading
observable.caveat: Historian logging proves receipt, not truth or effect on a controller.

scenarios.simulator_effect: Contaminates the historian's MQTT record only; reviewed SCADA code polls the intake PLC directly rather than consuming this sensor topic for control.
scenarios.hypothetical_physical_implication: Misleading telemetry could impair real operator judgement, but this simulator has no sensor-MQTT-to-actuator control path or demonstrated physical consequence.

defender_hypothesis.support: Sensor-topic historian record diverges from near-time SCADA Modbus intake level while the PLC remains reachable, with broker publication from the sensor identity.
defender_hypothesis.refute: Historian did not receive the message, or near-time PLC and sensor readings agree within cadence and precision.
defender_hypothesis.benign: Sensor cached its last reading after a PLC read failure, or ordinary timing difference between five-second polls.
